headline: Growth mindset believes abilities develop through effort—you can improve at almost anything
universal_truth: Talent is a starting point, not a ceiling; effort and learning extend what you can do
fun_facts: Research shows people with growth mindsets achieve more across academics, sports, and careers
The brain physically changes with learning—neural plasticity is real
Praising effort rather than talent develops growth mindset in children
discussion_questions: Where do you believe you can improve?
What skills have you developed through practice?
Where might a fixed mindset be limiting you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Can you get smarter? Can you become more creative? Can you develop skills you don't have? Growth mindset says yes—abilities develop through effort and learning. You're not fixed; you're growing.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Some people seem naturally talented while others struggle. Doesn't this prove abilities are fixed?

options.text: Talent sets starting points, not limits—some begin with more, but everyone can grow from where they start; effort and learning move the ceiling; what you work at, you improve at
options.response: Yes. The brain changes with practice. Skills develop with work. Natural talent matters for where you begin, not where you end. Growth mindset embraces the possibility of improvement.
Natural ability varies, but 'having it' usually includes years of practice that aren't visible—talent plus effort...

q1.title: Effort as Path
q1.script: Growth mindset sees effort as the path to mastery. Struggle isn't evidence of inability—it's the process of developing ability. Embrace the effort required to grow.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Effort as Path"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Learn from Failure
q2.script: Fixed mindset avoids failure to protect ego. Growth mindset sees failure as information—what worked, what didn't, what to try next. Failure teaches when you let it.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Yet Is Powerful
q3.script: Replace 'I can't' with 'I can't yet.' That single word transforms limitation into process. You're not unable; you're not yet able. Learning is the path from here to there.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Talent is a starting point, not a ceiling. Effort and learning extend what you can do. Believe in your ability to grow.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 347. Tomorrow, we'll explore when you think you can't change—fixed mindset. Until then, notice where you believe in growth.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Growth Mindset Check - Where Can You Grow?
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply growth mindset to personal development
growTrack.activity: Identify an area where you've believed you 'can't.' Add 'yet' to that belief. What would developing this ability require? What small step could you take toward growth?
